reason: A written Fourier-to-CM-norm derivation distinguishes the powered Stark unit from the primitive quartic packet and exposes two route-specific normalization gaps.

corrections.old_scope: the displayed norms of epsilon were identified as the primitive e=6 packets
corrections.new_scope: the powered-unit computations remain exact, but the primitive packet polynomials are those obtained after exact division of free-unit coordinates by three

corrections.old_scope: the packet was proved independently through e=8 and e=12
corrections.new_scope: the packet is proved through the natural e=8 route with |S|=3; the e=12 auxiliary-prime route is an exact cross-check but not a proof until finite valuations eliminate residual S-unit ambiguity
Engine B proves the packet; the Engine-C calculation is a normalization diagnostic until its fourth-root Fourier scaling is rederived

publication_effect: All three corrections are reflected in paper/effective-stark-results.tex. No public deposit or submission used the superseded scopes.
